cascade-susceptibility-cedar.label: Cascade experimental susceptibility index from the USGS daily-mean flow percentile at 12119000 (2000–2026, spanning 27 calendar years, n=130 values in the day-of-year window). Cedar at Renton sits below Chester Morse, which is operated for water supply with a limited flood role; the percentile is therefore partly an operations signal.

cascade-susceptibility-green-duwamish.label: Cascade experimental susceptibility index from the USGS daily-mean flow percentile at 12113000 (2000–2026, spanning 27 calendar years, n=130 values in the day-of-year window). Green near Auburn is below Howard Hanson, so the percentile partly measures USACE reservoir operations rather than basin wetness. Adding an unregulated inflow gauge above the dam is an open seed-data decision (design §2.3).

cascade-susceptibility-nooksack.label: Cascade experimental susceptibility index from the USGS daily-mean flow percentile at 12213100 (2000–2026, spanning 27 calendar years, n=130 values in the day-of-year window). Nooksack at Ferndale is unregulated but tidally influenced; whether the USGS daily mean is materially tide-contaminated has not been checked, so confidence is capped at moderate rather than high (design §7 item 6).

cascade-susceptibility-puyallup-white.label: Cascade experimental susceptibility index from the USGS daily-mean flow percentile at 12100490 (2000–2026, spanning 27 calendar years, n=130 values in the day-of-year window). White at R St is below Mud Mountain and has only a 17-year record (2010-2026), so the percentile is both operations-contaminated and thinly sampled. Adding an unregulated inflow gauge above the dam is an open seed-data decision (design §2.3).

cascade-susceptibility-skagit.label: Cascade experimental susceptibility index from the USGS daily-mean flow percentile at 12189500 (2000–2026, spanning 27 calendar years, n=130 values in the day-of-year window). The upper Skagit is regulated (Ross, Baker), so basin wetness is read from the unregulated Sauk (12189500, 1929-2026), which is often the dominant flood contributor (HYDROLOGY §2) — not from the Mount Vernon outlet.

cascade-susceptibility-snohomish-snoqual.label: Cascade experimental susceptibility index from the USGS daily-mean flow percentile at 12149000 (2000–2026, spanning 27 calendar years, n=130 values in the day-of-year window). Snoqualmie near Carnation is unregulated, so its day-of-year flow percentile is a basin state rather than an operating decision.
